title: Short Stuff: Runner's High
summary: Short Stuff episode on the runner's high. Josh and Chuck open with banter about feeling euphoric while running and Chuck's emotional reactions while watching The Price Is Right. They introduce flow state, a concept from psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, described as a focused mental state where performers feel effortless, channeled, and joyful. They note most athletes never experience a runner's high. The hosts then discuss the scientific debate: the 1970s running boom led researchers to credit endorphins, but endorphins apparently do not cross the blood-brain barrier, and the early claims were not checked until later, when they were found to be unsupported. A German study suggested running stimulates the endocannabinoid system, which does cross the blood-brain barrier and affects mood and anxiety, making it a plausible candidate. They conclude the runner's high may be real, a placebo or self-fulfilling effect, or simply not fully identified yet. The episode is an intro-and-content piece without a rerun designation.

segments.title: Opening banter and runner's high description
segments.summary: The hosts joke about feeling euphoric on a long run and describe the runner's high: feeling light, floating, and sometimes weeping with joy. Chuck says he has not had one but gets emotional watching The Price Is Right while running on a treadmill.

segments.title: Flow state
segments.summary: The hosts introduce flow state, a term coined by Hungarian-American psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi after interviewing athletes, musicians, and artists. It describes a focused mental state where performance feels effortless. They note most athletes have not experienced a runner's high and that flow state may be linked to it.

segments.title: Endorphin explanation and its problems
segments.summary: Researchers starting in the 1970s running boom proposed endorphins as the cause, since they act on opiate receptors to numb pain and produce morphine-like euphoria. The hosts say the endorphin idea was unchecked for decades and that endorphins apparently do not cross the blood-brain barrier, so the claim is doubtful.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: A sponsor message interrupts the episode.

segments.title: Endocannabinoids as a possible explanation
segments.summary: A German study suggested running stimulates the endocannabinoid system. Endocannabinoids can cross the blood-brain barrier and affect mood and anxiety, so they may explain the euphoric feeling in flow state. The hosts discuss marijuana's effect on anxiety, which varies by person.

segments.title: Conclusion and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts conclude the runner's high may be real, a placebo or self-fulfilling effect, or not yet fully identified. They say listeners will likely write in to defend it, then sign off.
